In this petition preferred under Section 407 of Cr.P.C, the petitioner is seeking transfer of CC.No.75/2020 pending before the II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC at Udupi to the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bengaluru.

sentences.text:
2. Heard both the sides and perused the material on record.
3.
Brief facts of the case are that, marriage of the petitioner and the respondent was solemnized on 23.04.2012 as per Hindu Rites and Customs, at Kunigal.
NC: 2024:KHC:14891 Both of them were practicing lawyers in Courts at Bengaluru at the time of their marriage.
The marriage was broken down in the year 2014 as there was some marital discord between them.
The respondent lodged a complaint, registered in Crime No.11/2019 at Women Police Station, Udupi against the petitioner and five others.
Charge-sheet was filed for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 323, 324, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
4. The transfer of the case from the Court of II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Udupi to the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bengaluru is sought on the following grounds.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. That CWs.1 to CW4, CWs.8 to CW12, CW15, CW17 and CW18 are from Bengaluru, CW13 is from Ramanagara, CW14 is from Tumakur.
Hence, 14 witnesses cited in the charge-sheet are from Sri.

sentences.text: Bengaluru and neighbouring district and remaining witnesses are from Udupi and out of them most of the witnesses are official NC: 2024:KHC:14891 witnesses.
Secondly, both the petitioner and the respondent are presently residing in Bengaluru.
Further, the petitioner has worked as a Civil Judge and JMFC in Udupi, where the present case is pending.

6. The petitioner/party-in-person would contend that he is ready to bare all the traveling expenses of the witnesses and submit that the divorce petition as well as petitions seeking restitution of conjugal rights and maintenance are also pending in Bengaluru.
7. The learned Counsel appearing for the respondent has filed statement of objections.
He has contended that the grounds now urged by the petitioner are not valid grounds to transfer the case from the Court at Udupi to Bengaluru.
He submitted that most of the witnesses are from Udupi and it will be difficult for them to travel all the way to Bengaluru.
He therefore submits that the prayer seeking transfer of the case from the Court at Udupi to Bengaluru can not be allowed.
Both the parties have raised various grounds on the merits of the case, which need not be adverted to, as the prayer made in this petition is to transfer the case.
9. It is not in dispute that the petitioner has worked as a Civil Judge and JMFC, Udupi, where the present case i.e., CC No.75/2020 is pending.

Even though the petitions seeking maintenance and restitution of conjugal rights initiated by the respondent and the divorce petition filed by the petitioner are pending in the Courts at Bengaluru, the respondent has vehemently opposed the prayer for transferring the present case from Udupi to Bengaluru.

10. Under Section 407 of Cr.P.C, whenever it is made to appear that a fair and impartial inquiry or trial cannot be held in any Criminal Court or that some question of law of unusual difficulty is likely to arise, or in the interest of the parties or witnesses considering the general convenience, Court can transfer any case from any NC: 2024:KHC:14891 Criminal Court to any other Courts of equal or superior jurisdiction etc.
11. In the present case, the petitioner had worked as a Civil Judge and JMFC in the Court at Udupi where the present case is pending.
An impression should not be created by allowing the case to be continued in the Court where the petitioner has earlier worked, that a fair and impartial trial was not held.
The respondent has not opposed the transfer of the case to any nearer Court where the present case is pending.
Both the parties have agreed to transfer the case from the Court of II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court at Udupi to the Court in Mangalore.
